Brilliant release by @VerneRobotics

V0.5, an open-weight world action model, that looks through cameras and outputs the next second of arm, gripper and mobile-base motion. 

The big deal is that it learned new industrial tasks from under 2 hours of demonstrations.

> Robot models usually stumble when a room changes. With clutter and new lighting that neither model trained on, Verne Robotics’ V0.5 lost 7.6 points in simulation, while Physical Intelligence’s π0.5 lost 24.7.

> On RoboTwin 2.0, randomized clutter, lighting and textures cut V0.5 from 81.0% to 73.4% in Verne’s tests, while Physical Intelligence’s π0.5 fell from 70.7% to 46.0%.

> Built on the Wan2.2 video generator, V0.5 learned from over 1.7M demonstrations to predict upcoming camera frames alongside the motion producing them.

posts.text_zh:
Verne Robotics 放出了很亮眼的 V0.5：开源权重世界动作模型，吃摄像头画面，输出未来约 1 秒的手臂、夹爪与移动底座动作。

关键点是：新工业任务只需不到 2 小时示教就能学会。

机器人模型换房间常翻车。在训练未见过的杂乱与新光照下，V0.5 仿真掉 7.6 分，Physical Intelligence 的 π0.5 掉 24.7 分。

RoboTwin 2.0 上，随机杂乱/光照/纹理让 V0.5 从 81.0% 降到 73.4%，π0.5 从 70.7% 掉到 46.0%。

底座基于 Wan2.2 视频生成，用超过 170 万条示教，同时预测未来画面与产生这些画面的动作。

METR estimates that Anthropic is currently making progress in the capabilities of its models about twice as fast as it used to, and that the use of AI itself is driving a large part of this acceleration.

Independent evaluator METR found that Anthropic’s model benchmark scores have improved 1.9x faster since October 2025.  

METR estimates that AI may account for around 80% of the current acceleration, though that estimate is highly uncertain.
posts.text_short: METR estimates that Anthropic is currently making progress in the capabilities of its models about twice as fast as it used to, and that the use of AI itself is driving a large pa…
posts.text_zh:
METR 估计，Anthropic 目前提升模型能力的速度大约是过去的两倍，而且很大一部分加速来自用 AI 本身做研发。

独立评估方 METR 发现，自 2025 年 10 月以来 Anthropic 模型基准分数的提升速度约为之前的 1.9 倍。

METR 估计 AI 可能贡献了当前加速的约 80%，但该估计不确定性很高。
posts.summary_zh: METR 估计 Anthropic 能力进步约加快 1.9 倍，其中约 80% 或由 AI 自身参与研发驱动（不确定性高）

I spent 20,000 dollars in API credits having different AI models play each other at Blood on the Clocktower (a Mafia or Werewolf type social deception game).

The results were fascinating. Models have gotten much better over the course of this year at creative on-the-spot scheming and bluffing, and also at reasoning as a team to break apart these underground conspiracies.

I go through some of the most standout games these AIs played in this video. The new models are getting pretty good.  If my friends pulled off some of these moves while we were playing, I’d give them a fist bump.

Fwiw, OpenAI’s newer models are much better than Anthropic’s at this game.

You can see the full benchmark at the website, and I’ve also made it so that you and your friends can play again the AIs: http://clocktowerbench.com

Nanbeige has released Nanbeige4.3-33B, an open weights model matching Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 with stronger terminal use but weaker knowledge

@Nanbeige is the foundation model research team at BOSS Zhipin, the Chinese recruitment platform operated by Kanzhun Limited. Its dense 33B reasoning model is open weights under Apache 2.0, with text input and output only, a 524K-token context window, and is small enough to run locally on a laptop.

Key results:

➤ Competitive results at ~30B total parameters. Nanbeige4.3-33B and Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) both score 20, compared with 6 for Muse Glimmer (high, 30B).

➤ Terminal use and physics reasoning are relative strengths. Nanbeige scores 30% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 16% on CritPt v2's Hard Subset, vs. 6% and 4% respectively for Qwen3.8 27B.

➤ Different strengths to Qwen3.8 27B despite the same overall score. Nanbeige beats Qwen3.8 27B on AutomationBench-AA (53% vs. 48%), but trails on AA-Briefcase v1.1 (1162 vs. 1391 Elo), FrontierCode 2.0 (11% vs. 15%) and HLE-Diamond (7% vs. 15%).

➤ High abstention and low hallucination rates on Omniscience. Nanbeige scores -4 on AA-Omniscience v1.1 vs. -6 for Qwen3.8 27B, with a hallucination rate of 18% vs. 29%. It answers fewer questions correctly (12% vs. 17%) and declines 71% of questions.

➤ Similar intelligence with more output tokens per task. Nanbeige used 158K output tokens per Intelligence Index task vs. 110K for Qwen3.8 27B, about 44% more.

Additional model details:

➤ Type: Open weights reasoning (Apache 2.0 license)

➤ Size: 33B total parameters (dense)

➤ Modalities: Text input and output only

➤ Context window: 524K

➤ API availability: No confirmed public first- or third-party APIs

Answering some common q's:

1. Is this really cheaper than Higgsfield?

Yes - for Seedance 2.5 and most other models.

If you have better prices from somewhere else no worries - you can add any API key to Voyager.

2. How the f*** are you guys affording this?

We're not losing money on this - we're just not marking it up...

Enjoy it while it lasts 😅

JK: we make money from a hosted version of our harness (similar to Hermes) and from team features.

Reach out to me if you're a company, studio or pro who wants to learn more.

3. How do you reduce the number of generations?

Voyager is a harness for creative work. It's not just an AI video generator.

It runs on your desktop like Codex/Claude - so it can use apps like Blender for pre-vis, Da Vinci resolve for editing. It can storyboard, do internet research, make character sheets and more.

By the time you call an AI video model, Voyager will help you do the pre-work to get a good result.

If you need to make changes, it can edit it in many ways and not just re-gen.

4. Where can I sign up?

http://voyager.so - make sure you download the desktop app for the full experience. You can also try in browser.

5. I have so many questions

Join our discord :) https://discord.gg/voyagerai

Marvel spends $5M on a close-up tech shot for a few seconds of screen time. VFX team, a full render farm, weeks in post for one gadget that looks real.

this creator made the same sci-fi gadget on a laptop for $7.

a little desktop machine paints a tiny 3D cherry blossom onto a fingernail by itself, done in seconds like it's the most normal thing in the world.

the clip pulled 5.2M views in two days, and the comments are split between people asking where to buy it and people swearing it's impossible.

the details that sell it:

> the needle tip floats just over the nail while a soft green light glows inside the chamber
> the raised flower catches tiny highlights and shadows that match the room
> the preview on the screen lines up almost exactly with the finished nail

the tools behind it:

> Kimi K3 wrote the scene, the machine motion, and the camera
> Kling 3.0 built the needle movement and the glow in the chamber
> Seedance 2.5 handled the 3D flower, the highlights, and the micro-shadows
> ElevenLabs made the soft machine hum and the room sound
> CapCut did the close-up zoom, the color, and the export

a real version of this needs a prop team, a working rig, a product designer, and weeks of VFX cleanup to make it believable.

this one got made in a single sitting by one person with no crew.

i wrote up the whole workflow, from the tools to how you get paid, in the article below
